extracted.intended_audience: United States Congress, federal officials, and the American public (1861)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Abraham Lincoln's July–August 1861 executive messages, memoranda, orders, and a proclamation addressing rebellion, military policy, prisoner treatment, troop mobilization, and related administrative actions during the opening months of the Civil War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of the writ of habeas corpus
rubrics_metrics.description: "The provision of the Constitution that 'the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended, unless when, in cases of rebellion or invasion, the public safety may require it,' is equivalent to a provision--is a provision--that such privilege may be suspended when, in case of rebellion or invasion, the public safety does require it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be exercised in cases of rebellion or invasion when public safety requires it; the Constitution is silent as to which branch must exercise the power, and in dangerous emergencies the executive may act when Congress cannot be promptly convened; authority should be used sparingly and will be subject to further legal opinion and possible legislation by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilization scale recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is now recommended that you give the legal means for making this contest a short and decisive one: that you place at the control of the government for the work at least four hundred thousand men and $400,000,000."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification given (men ≈ one-tenth of those of proper ages in hostile regions; money < 1/23 of country wealth); presented as legislative request to empower executive and facilitate a decisive, short campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the blockade effective
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the plan for making the blockade effective be pushed forward with all possible despatch."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urgent directive to prioritize and expedite the implementation of the naval blockade of insurrectionary districts to impair enemy supplies and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drill and discipline volunteer forces at Fort Monroe
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the volunteer forces at Fort Monroe and vicinity under General Butler be constantly drilled, disciplined, and instructed without more for the present."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate focus on training and discipline for forces in that locality before other actions; emphasizes preparation over further redeployment for the short term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold Baltimore firmly but judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let Baltimore be held as now, with a gentle but firm and certain hand."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain control of critical border cities with measured firmness—balance steadiness and restraint to secure position without unnecessary provocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen and secure forces under Patterson or Banks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the force now under Patterson or Banks be strengthened and made secure in its position."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforce existing commands where necessary to ensure defensible, stable positions before further operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Western Virginia forces follow General McClellan's orders
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the forces in Western Virginia act till further orders according to instructions or orders from General McClellan."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign operational control and continuity by deferring to the designated theater commander until new directives are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fremont to accelerate Western operations (focus Missouri)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let [General Fremont] push forward his organization and operations in the West as rapidly as possible, giving rather special attention to Missouri."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to rapid organization and action in the Western theater with special emphasis on stabilizing Missouri.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganize forces from Manassas (except three-months men)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the forces late before Manassas, except the three-months men, be reorganized as rapidly as possible in their camps here and about Arlington."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid reconstitution and reorganization of units previously engaged, excluding short-term enlistees, to restore effective field forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge three-months forces who decline longer service
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the three-months forces who decline to enter the longer service be discharged as rapidly as circumstances will permit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the enlistment terms of short-term volunteers; discharge promptly those who opt not to re-enlist for longer service to maintain force cohesion and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring new volunteer forces forward into camps
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the new volunteer forces be brought forward as fast as possible, and especially into the camps on the two sides of the river here."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urgent movement and concentration of newly raised volunteers into staging camps near the capital/front to facilitate organization and deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize and hold Manassas Junction and Strasburg; secure lines
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let Manassas Junction (or some point on one or other of the railroads near it) and Strasburg be seized, and permanently held, with an open line from Washington to Manassas, and an open line from Harper's Ferry to Strasburg..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic seizure and permanent control of key railway and communication points to ensure secure lines between Washington, Manassas, Harper's Ferry, and Strasburg.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct joint movements from Cairo and Cincinnati
rubrics_metrics.description: "This done, a joint movement from Cairo on Memphis; and from Cincinnati on East Tennessee."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate multi-pronged offensives from river and interior bases to strike strategic targets (Cairo→Memphis; Cincinnati→East Tennessee) following securing of lines and staging areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Indian regiments conditional on Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have agreed, and do agree, that the two Indian regiments named within shall be accepted if the act of Congress shall admit it. Let there be no further question about it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of volunteer regiments contingent upon statutory authorization; indicates deference to Congressional admission while expressing executive concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for lodging and sustenance of political prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Marshals of the United States in the vicinity of forts where political prisoners are held will supply decent lodging and sustenance for such prisoners unless they shall prefer to provide in those respects for themselves, in which case they will be allowed to do so by the commanding officer in charge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational instruction to marshals to ensure humane provisioning for political prisoners, with allowance for prisoner self-provisioning if preferred; order approved and to be transmitted to relevant officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of 'armed neutrality' policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the border States... there are those who favor a policy which they call 'armed neutrality'... it would tie the hands of Union men and freely pass supplies from among them to the insurrectionists... very injurious in effect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative judgment that an armed neutrality stance would effectively aid secessionists and damage Union interests; thus it should be opposed as a policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No constitutional right of secession; duty to preserve the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that no State has power to destroy the Union: States have only powers reserved by the Constitution; the Union created the States; secession is revolutionary, not lawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal-political standard underpinning use of federal power: preserve the Union, protect loyal citizens, and employ necessary means (including war power) to prevent disintegration and to maintain the republican form of government guaranteed by the Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for accepting state regiments (New Jersey example)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Together with the regiments of three years' volunteers which the government already has in service in your State, enough to make eight in all, if tendered in a reasonable time, will be accepted... the new regiments to be taken, as far as convenient, from the three months' men and officers just discharged, and to be organized, equipped, and sent forward as fast as single regiments are ready, On the same terms as were those already in the service from that State."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural conditions for accepting additional state regiments: timing reasonable, use experienced men when convenient, organize/equip/send forward rapidly, and accept under same terms as existing regiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for Congressional legislation to support exhibitions and fisheries cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmit correspondence and recommend 'such legislation by Congress at this session as may be necessary' to enable US participation in an international industrial exhibition and to provide for a commissioner regarding fisheries cooperation with Great Britain and France.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recommendation that Congress enact enabling statutes to permit executive participation in international exhibitions and joint commissions for fisheries inquiry/cooperation.
